mappings.note: Two demands: what aerenchyma is structurally (large interconnected air cavities) and what that buys an aquatic plant (buoyancy, gas store for survival). Structure first, role second - the 3-mark version of the two 1-mark aerenchyma items, which each take only one of the pair.

The scored explanation is what companion cells do for enucleate sieve tubes (role); LO-1 second because the tissue must first be identified as phloem from a diagram, which is the xylem/phloem and simple/complex discrimination.
Primary protective functions of the epidermis lead (role), with C-4.2-LO-2 for the second half, where a structural secretion - the waxy cuticle - has to be tied to water retention.
The stem ends on how phloem's cellular nature differs from xylem's - living against dead - which is the xylem/phloem line in LO-1; C-4.2-LO-3 for the composition-and-function half.

Asks for structure and function of intestinal epithelium explicitly, so both outcomes are earned: tall columnar cells with microvilli (structure) serving absorption, and the general covering/lining role of epithelium.

One variable - number of cell layers - set against two functional demands, wear resistance versus rapid exchange. The purest structure-to-function item in the chapter; no tissue has to be named or differentiated.

The classification argument runs on the structural criterion (cells suspended in an extracellular matrix) and then on the connective role blood performs. Not C-4.2-LO-4: no organisation level is at stake, only membership of a tissue class.

The comparison is asked on two axes named in the stem: what each connects (role) and how flexible each is (structural property). LO-1 cannot take it - tendon versus ligament is not among the pairs it lists.

The stem states the target outright: structural differences in the matrix and how they affect physical properties. Calcified against protein-and-sugar matrix, hence rigid against firm-but-flexible. Single clean structure-to-function item.

Remove-the-component-and-predict form: uncontrolled bleeding follows from the loss of the clotting role. Same outcome as the plain platelet recall item in part 5, reached by consequence rather than by statement.

The claim to be refuted misassigns voluntary control to smooth muscle, which is the striated/smooth/cardiac discrimination (LO-1); C-4.2-LO-3 for correctly assigning peristalsis to smooth muscle as its role in the gut.

Dendrites as receivers and axon as transmitter is structure-to-function for the parts of one cell. The diagram half is unmapped: this frame has no outcome covering the drawing of labelled biological diagrams.

A head-to-head comparison of two of the three muscle types on exactly the axes LO-1 implies - cell structure and voluntary control. Nothing beyond the discrimination is asked, so it stays on one code.

Single tissue rather than a comparison, so LO-1 is not used here: the demand is its structural features and then its continuous role in the body. That is the split rule against the skeletal-versus-cardiac item above, which is a comparison and takes LO-1.

Requires several tissues - bone, muscle, tendon, ligament, cartilage - to be related to one another to produce movement, which is the correlation C-5.3-LO-2 asks for. C-4.2-LO-4 second because the first half asks what constitutes an organ system, a level of organisation.
The scored half is how hinge movement differs from ball and socket - a joint-type discrimination. The diagram half has no home in this frame.

Protective role of the rib cage leads, as in the two shorter rib-cage items; C-4.2-LO-2 is added here and not there because this version asks why flexible cartilage is needed, a structure-to-function step the others do not reach.
Identifies a pivot joint and then contrasts its movement with fixed joints - two joint types from the LO-1 list, compared. No role or structural reasoning beyond the classification.

Same demands as the Steward sequencing MCQ in part 2 and mapped identically on purpose: reconstructing the steps of an investigation (C8.2) about the frontier concept of totipotency (C7.1). Written recall versus MCQ ordering is a format difference, not an outcome difference.

Split from the two sequencing items: this one asks why each medium component was necessary, which is reasoning about the design (C8.2), and then what the result proved, which is drawing and naming a finding from a result (C-8.2-LO-3). C7.1 for totipotency itself.

Part (a) is the plant/animal tissue difference (LO-1); parts (b) and (c) are the three meristems by location and the consequence of losing the apical one, both role-of-tissue. LO-6 rejected: part (c) is a predicted consequence, with nothing set up, performed or measured.

Earns three codes because the stem names three separate axes of comparison: cell wall composition and living nature (structure), exact function in plants (role), across the collenchyma/sclerenchyma pair LO-1 lists.

Part (a) is the protective role of the epidermis; part (b) asks how that same basic structure is modified in desert plants and underground roots to meet different demands, which is structure-to-function. Broader than the cuticle-only item earlier in this part.

Part (a) asks for the broad functions of epithelium (role); parts (b) and (c) are squamous versus columnar structure and why skin must be stratified, both structure-to-function. LO-1 does not cover epithelial subtypes.

Part (b) contrasts xylem and phloem function, the pair named in LO-1; part (c) asks why companion cells are essential to sieve tubes, a role within a complex tissue. The diagram in part (a) is not covered by any outcome here.
